title: Yarrow compress for varicose veins
subtitle: A cooling external compress of Achillea millefolium for the aching and heaviness of varicose veins
excerpt: Yarrow compress is a cloth soaked in a strong cold yarrow infusion and applied to the legs over varicose veins for 15 to 20 minutes. A traditional toning and astringent external preparation for the aching, heaviness, and tenderness of varicose veins. Used cold, not hot, heat worsens venous congestion. The tannins and flavonoids in yarrow have a toning action on the vein walls. Prepare in batches and refrigerate the liquid for up to 24 hours.
sourceNotes: Maud Grieve, A Modern Herbal (1931), yarrow entry, Botanical.com. Traditional use of Achillea millefolium as a vulnerary and venous tonic documented in European herbalism from the 16th century; Culpeper, Complete Herbal (1653).

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The strained yarrow liquid keeps 24 hours in the refrigerator. Prepare in a larger batch if using daily.

glossaryTerms.definition: A herb rich in tannins that causes the contraction and tightening of soft tissues on contact, toning blood vessel walls, reducing local inflammation, and decreasing permeability. Yarrow's tannins make it one of the most useful astringent herbs for venous conditions.

content.text: Yarrow compress is a cloth wrung out in a strong cold yarrow infusion and applied directly to the legs over varicose veins for 15 to 20 minutes. A traditional

external preparation for the heaviness, aching, and tenderness that accompany varicose veins. The cold temperature is deliberate and important, cold contracts the vessel walls and reduces blood pooling in the veins. a hot application would worsen venous congestion. The yarrow's tannins and flavonoids provide additional toning action on the vein wall tissue. Applied in the afternoon when the legs are most tired, with the feet elevated during the treatment.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body: Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor before use. Full precautions are in the 'When not to use' section.

content.text: Place 30 g of dried yarrow in a heatproof bowl. Pour 500 ml of just-boiled water over the herb. Cover and steep for 20 minutes.
Strain through a sieve into a clean bowl. Allow to cool to room temperature, then refrigerate until cold (at least 30 minutes).
Elevate the legs on a pillow. Soak a folded muslin cloth or flannel in the cold yarrow liquid. Wring out so it is damp but not dripping.
Lay the compress over the affected vein areas of the leg. Keep in place for 15 to 20 minutes, rewetting the cloth if it warms up. Re-soak in the cold liquid if needed.
Once daily, ideally in the afternoon. Use regularly for 4 weeks, combined with leg elevation and movement breaks during prolonged sitting or standing.
The strained yarrow liquid keeps 24 hours in a sealed container in the refrigerator. Prepare a larger batch and use over two days.
When not to use this remedy

Do not apply to skin ulcers, broken skin, or areas of infection. See a doctor for significant leg swelling or skin hardening over varicose veins. Seek urgent care for acute leg pain that comes with warmth and redness on one side. This may be a DVT, which is a medical emergency.
